t: You're standing outside the Sir Alexander Fleming, a pub in Paddington that takes its name from the Scottish physician and microbiologist. Fleming matters because in 1928 he discovered what was later named benzylpenicillin, from the mould Penicillium rubens. It was the first antibiotic substance, and it has been described as the single greatest victory ever achieved over disease. In 1945 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Howard Florey and Ernst Chain for the discovery of penicillin and its curative effect in various infectious diseases. So raise a glass to him.
